stale_wal_incident.symptom: the Jarvis target state.db raised sqlite3.DatabaseError 'database disk image is malformed' on normal open; the byte-identical source DB opens clean with immutable=1
stale_wal_incident.cause: the target carried a stale state.db-wal (840512 bytes) whose frames belong to TWO epochs: 2 frames with the current WAL-header salt (7a2c8974/654112d8) and 202 frames of an older epoch (7a2c8973/e28ccfb4). SQLite replaying the WAL hits the older-epoch frames and fails. The main DB file itself is intact (integrity ok, 5 sessions, 4786 messages).
stale_wal_incident.evidence: wal header salt 7a2c8974/654112d8; frame 0 pgno 13 and frame 1 pgno 14 carry the current salt; frames 2..203 carry the older salt
stale_wal_incident.repair: applied ONLY the two current-epoch frames onto a copy of the main DB (the standard epoch-validity rule), verified integrity ok with identical row counts (5 sessions / 4786 messages, unchanged from the immutable view), replaced the main DB with that clean copy and removed the stale sidecars
stale_wal_incident.result: profiles/telegram-bot-8812646969/state.db now opens clean in normal mode; sha256 d2737f3b83dca11d9e63e6030f38bae9a12a8c0bd97f68030715c2c709bd6b0c; no data lost (row counts equal to the source's immutable view)
stale_wal_incident.no_live_process_touched: the gateway serves only the default profile and holds no open handle on these files; the merge happened while no agent was active (active_agents 0)
